title: Scaling Makes It Possible: How Large Models Master Impossible Languages
abstract: arXiv:2611.02015v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While language models (LMs) excel in natural language tasks, their ability to learn impossible languages--those that violate the structural, cognitive, or logical constraints that make human languages learnable and functional--remains debatable. This controversy is further fueled by a divide between linguistic theorists and empirical researchers working with small-scale LMs. To address this controversy, we introduce semantic coherence. This concept measures how effectively semantic information is expressed in language structures and examines the learning capabilities of LMs across multiple scales. By fine-tuning billion-parameter LMs on impossible language samples, we demonstrate that larger LMs achieve similar performance on impossible and possible languages, whereas million-parameter LMs exhibit significant degradation when trained on impossible languages. translated_title: 规模化使其成为可能：大模型如何掌握“不可能语言”
translated_abstract: 尽管语言模型（LM）在自然语言任务中表现出色，但其学习“不可能语言”——即那些违反了使人类语言可学习、可运作的结构性、认知性或逻辑性约束的语言——的能力仍存在争议。语言学理论家与使用小规模语言模型进行实证研究的研究者之间的分歧进一步加剧了这一争论。为解决这一争议，我们提出了“语义连贯性”（semantic coherence）这一概念，用于衡量语义信息在语言结构中被表达的有效程度，并考察了语言模型在多个参数规模下的学习能力。通过在“不可能语言”样本上微调十亿参数级的语言模型，我们证明较大规模的语言模型在“不可能语言”和“可能语言”上能够取得相近的性能，而百万参数级的语言模型在“不可能语言”上训练时则表现出显著的性能退化，且这一性能差距随语义复杂度的增加而不断扩大。我们进一步表明……
tldr: 该论文提出“语义连贯性”概念，揭示出十亿参数级的大语言模型能够像掌握可能语言一样掌握违反人类语言约束的“不可能语言”，而百万参数级小模型则显著失败，且性能差距随语义复杂度增加而扩大。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "semantic coherence" and demonstrates that billion-parameter language models learn impossible languages nearly as well as possible languages, while million-parameter models degrade significantly, with the performance gap widening as semantic complexity increases.
